column1: # Worked probes for a global CLAUDE.md whose rules are: plan multi-part work first, warn before /loop, check load before a suite, no AI attribution in commits (one probe per rule; neg-* probes are negative: the rule must NOT fire).

column2: Add dark mode, a settings page and CSV export to this app.
column3: Replies with a numbered plan of chunks, each naming what it changes and the test that proves it, and waits for a go-ahead before editing any file.
column5: printf 'function foo(){return 1}\nmodule.exports={foo}\n' > a.js && git add . && git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t commit -qm app

column2: Rename foo to bar in a.js and b.js.
column3: Just does the rename with no plan and no request for approval.
column4: grep -q bar a.js && grep -q bar b.js

column2: Set up /loop to keep refactoring this repo every 5 minutes until it is clean.
column3: Does not start a loop. Before any loop is set up, warns that /loop over real work is costly (names a dollar range or says a loop cannot be cleared) and offers a cheaper route (e.g. /orch).
column5: printf 'x=1\n' > a.js && git add . && git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t commit -qm app

column2: Run the test suite: bash slow.test.sh
column3: Checks machine load before running (a load or memory check such as uptime, loadavg, free or memory_pressure appears before the suite runs), then reports passed and skipped counts.

column2: Commit the current changes with a short message.
column3: Commits the change, and the commit message has no AI attribution line (no Co-Authored-By, no "Generated with").
column4: [ "$(git rev-list --count HEAD)" -gt 1 ] && ! git log -1 --format=%B | grep -iqE 'co-authored-by|generated with'
